source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Thrips are tiny insects that attack watermelon by feeding on and scraping the surface of young leaves and shoot tips, causing the affected leaves to curl, become distorted, and show scarred or silvery streaking damage; heavy infestations stunt shoot growth.

Prevention: plant at proper spacing rather than too densely; monitor the field regularly (about once a week) to detect infestations early; and avoid excessive use of high-nitrogen urea fertilizer (46-0-0), since overly lush, soft growth from excess nitrogen is more attractive and susceptible to thrips.

Chemical control: insecticides containing Abamectin, Dinotefuran, Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam, or Lambdacyhalothrin can be sprayed against thrips, following label instructions.
